# History of the NORMAL STAR/FLOW getter admission gap

The same-path C2 rejection is older than the canonicalization changes. Commit `c347ff8bb74e78062c3ae8162c8a0e9a2074f398` introduced it on 2026-10-29. The C2 policy has identical bytes at `52f32dd4`, `8331bf9e`, `4182adae` and current. This does not prove that the same small program failed at each revision. A saved NORMAL relation can answer a call before C2, and earlier storage can lose guidance before this cell is reached.

This audit ran no JVM, compiler, Gradle task, analyzer, Lean check or real-project baseline. It changed no repository file. The [JSON evidence](history-audit.json) contains 48 source, diff and historical control artifacts, exact revision/path/hash anchors, current snapshot extracts and 65 passing static checks. The new 52f program control is prepared but unrun.

## What changed, and when

| Revision or commit | Source result |
|---|---|
| `f945f92c5ae554ff4f5fc7696ee5a269210478bb` | No bidirectional package, C2 policy, driver fixture or loop reproducer exists. This is the older IFDS analyzer. Its summary handler uses `EdgeRefinement` and suffix concatenation. It cannot execute this fixture without a different harness. |
| Parent of `c347ff8` | `ap/Reference.kt:150–160`: a FLOW demand calls `overlap`, then `flowForm`. For `d=arg0.g.ANY/FLOW`, `a=arg0.g.STAR/FLOW`, overlap is true and the returned pattern is `arg0.g.STAR/FLOW`. `DemandResultCoverage.kt` calls this emitter directly. |
| `c347ff8` | New `RestrictedInitialPolicy.kt:25–29` returns null for equal paths, demanded ANY and actual STAR. The same commit routes scalar emission through this policy and adds FLOW pair normalization. This is the first source change of this scalar cell, not a measured whole-program first failure. |
| `e090118e5f9603f1973c0578a3e04998035f4508` | Current restricted call subscription/start now requires nonempty C2 initials. Saved NORMAL replay is moved into an explicit caller path before that gate. Earlier code subscribed first and replayed records inside the subscription manager. |
| `52f32dd437d438aec4a700a02c18d94c31d58093` | Both the rejection and caller gate already exist. The point store also subtracts child MAY memberships under a stored MAY prefix: `ap/Groups.kt:169–186`. |
| `8331bf9e326ddd1bd5083dbc50456963d6b26b52` | Adds canonical packets, aligned NORMAL relation subsumption, atomic persistent-record indexes, and role-specific strict-ancestor STAR matching. It does not change this C2 policy. |
| `4182adae6152b4600a5401b78512b2b5b581998f` | Repairs FLOW guide coordinate retention in three storage files. C2, ordinary summary matching and the call replay/gate code remain unchanged. |
| Current storage repair over `e6fbda8e1` | Repairs the recorded concrete B2 point loss. C2 still rejects the F3 getG cell. The native program completes and accepts run 5 with zero NORMAL reports. |

All four post-52f C2 copies have SHA-256 `dcbaee551ecdae33590c56ef0154bfd0ef419c8c8fa3dc7b38127006a73ad44e`.

The fixture itself was added in `2ff3db70d124af37cdc352156677fab2aa546a72`. Its source is unchanged since that commit: SHA-256 `8165143d74e738d69bd36d525b60a0b8948d8836b1803abc0f52bbfa8ba5ec59`. Existing sealed 8331 checks, with and without one canonical-prefix subtraction, both reach/complete/accept 5/5/5 and miss the report. Thus this miss predates the later FLOW and concrete storage repairs. Those checks do not establish a 52f result.

## Can a saved getter summary avoid C2?

Yes, conditionally. Both 52f and current call `replayPersistedSummaries` before `emitRestrictedInitials`. A same-direction saved NORMAL row

```text
arg0.g.STAR/FLOW -> ret.STAR/FLOW NORMAL
```

can match the recorded actual `arg0.g.STAR/FLOW NORMAL` at the same path in both versions. That read does not need a new C2 initial or a new getG actor. The current capture does not enumerate the complete persistent-record directory, so it cannot establish the historical presence or absence of that saved row.

The 8331 matching change is narrower. In 52f, an actual `arg0.STAR/FLOW` can be selected by a deeper saved entry `arg0.g.STAR/FLOW` through strict-ancestor STAR selection. Current `SAVED_DIRECT` and `CURRENT` matching disable that selection. `OPPOSITE_RECORD` retains it, with native record guards. This change does not affect the recorded equal-path `g.STAR` cell. A historical shortcut through a coarser actual is possible in source; its execution is unobserved here.

The aligned NORMAL relation law also has a precise bound. If a shorter input covers a longer input with residual `g`, it appends `g` to the shorter output paths. Such a cover cannot directly remove the getter row whose output is the empty `ret` path: no ordinary `outputPath ++ [g]` is empty. Other rows, same-input joins and persistence changes remain separate questions. This is a local source calculation, not a proof of all historical store contents.

The current F3 evidence remains exact: getF returns `ret.g.STAR/FLOW NORMAL` under `arg0.f.g.STAR/FLOW`; the mapper processes `gotF.g.STAR/FLOW NORMAL`; getG has only `arg0.g.ANY/FLOW -> ret.ANY/FLOW`, no actor and zero processed inputs. The bound getG actual and null C2 result are source-derived from those records, not a rejected-C2 callback.

## Prepared authoritative 52f control

The [control directory](same-program-52f-control/ROOT-COMMANDS.txt) contains a pristine full 52f source snapshot, a unique optional task and a separate harness. All 5,279 tracked blobs, totaling 228,625,675 bytes, match the Git tree. There are no gitlinks or submodules. The four fixture helper files are byte-identical at 52f and current.

The sole harness change replaces the absent post-8331 `SpatialCanonicalKt` CodeSource print with the stable `ApOps` CodeSource print. The analyzed IR, rules, IDs, source, observation, CFG, calls, FULL mode, limits `1,1,2,3,...,9`, budget and assertions stay unchanged. The exact two-line diagnostic diff is sealed. Provider and logback bytes match the current capture. No current source is put on the historical runtime classpath.

Root must run the sealed command, then verify the historical ApOps class origin, source seals and actual classpath. The child uses 1 GiB, one CPU and 20 seconds; Java 21 and a 2 GiB in-process Gradle build use a fresh registry. Compilation, dependency resolution, build operation without `.git`, and native completion are still unverified. A compile or setup failure is not an analyzer result.

If 52f reports the observation, a later change exposed the missing route; the next useful evidence is its actual saved getter rows and matched input, not a policy guess. If 52f also misses it, the miss predates 8331, but its first executed loss can still differ: 52f already has the early MAY-prefix subtraction. Only then should a bounded per-run observer compare saved records, complete paired demands, processed getter inputs and output layers under each full runtime. No partial source substitution is an authoritative historical control.

No new C2 rule is selected. This audit does not establish a Conductor cause, native program recovery, progress or termination, and it does not rerun the fixed f945 real-project baseline.

package org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.engine

import org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.ap.*
import org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.store.Record

/** Read the previous-run store on every original offer, without live input history. */
internal fun replayPersistedSummaries(
    config: RunConfig,
    ops: ApOps,
    part: Subscription,
    applier: SummaryApplier,
    statistics: N2Statistics? = null,
) {
    check(config.restricted && !part.zeroOnly)
    val records = config.records
    val direction = config.direction
    val mode = config.mode
    val cancellation = ops.manager.cancellation
    statistics?.persistedReplayStarted()
    val seen = HashSet<Record>()
    val seenViews = HashMap<RecordLeafView, Boolean>()
    for (leaf in ops.leaves(part.added)) {
        cancellation.checkpoint()
        for (record in records.byEntry(part.callee, leaf)) {
            cancellation.checkpoint()
            statistics?.persistedReplayCandidate()
            if (record.direction != direction || !seen.add(record)) continue
            val added = ops.satisfying(part.added, record.premise, mode, record = true) ?: continue
            statistics?.persistedReplayMatched()
            applier.applyRecord(part.copy(added = added), record)
        }
        for (record in records.byExit(part.callee, leaf)) {
            cancellation.checkpoint()
            statistics?.persistedReplayCandidate()
            if (record.direction == direction) continue
            record.forEachReversedAt(leaf) { view, nonSubsumable ->
                cancellation.checkpoint()
                val previous = seenViews[view]
                if (previous == true || previous == false && !nonSubsumable) return@forEachReversedAt
                seenViews[view] = previous == true || nonSubsumable
                val added = ops.satisfying(part.added, view.premise, mode, record = true)
                    ?: return@forEachReversedAt
                statistics?.persistedReplayMatched()
                applier.applyRecordView(part.copy(added = added), view, nonSubsumable)
            }
        }
    }
}

import sys, subprocess, json, hashlib, datetime, os
from pathlib import Path
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
root=Path(__file__).resolve().parent
repo=Path('/drive-testcomp/opentaint-go-rules/opentaint-w3')
phase=sys.argv[1]
assert phase == 'full'
coreTask=':opentaint-dataflow-core:opentaint-dataflow:test'
jvmTask=':opentaint-dataflow-core:opentaint-jvm-dataflow:test'
cmd=['./gradlew','-I',str(root.parent/'test-controls.init.gradle'),'--no-daemon','--console=plain','--max-workers=1','--no-build-cache',
 '-Dorg.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx2g -XX:ActiveProcessorCount=2','-Dorg.gradle.daemon.registry.base='+str(root/'registry'),'-Pkotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process']
if phase=='repro':
 cmd+=['-I',str(repo/'scripts/loop-boundary-reproducer.init.gradle'),':opentaint-dataflow-core:opentaint-dataflow:runLoopBoundaryPrecisionReproducer']
else:
 cmd+=[coreTask]
 if phase!='full': cmd+=['--tests','org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.ConcreteGuideStorageTest','--tests','org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.ProtectedStorageCoordinatesTest']
 if phase=='full':cmd+=[jvmTask,'--continue']
files=[repo/'core/opentaint-dataflow-core/opentaint-dataflow'/p for p in [
 'src/main/kotlin/org/opentaint/dataflow/bidi/ap/Groups.kt','src/main/kotlin/org/opentaint/dataflow/bidi/ap/SpatialCanonical.kt',
 'src/main/kotlin/org/opentaint/dataflow/bidi/store/DiagonalRelations.kt',
 'src/test/kotlin/org/opentaint/dataflow/bidi/ConcreteGuideStorageTest.kt','src/test/kotlin/org/opentaint/dataflow/bidi/ProtectedStorageCoordinatesTest.kt','src/test/kotlin/org/opentaint/dataflow/bidi/ProtectedAdmissionDataBridgeTest.kt']]
sha=lambda p:hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
receipt={'phase':phase,'startedUTC':datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),'command':cmd,
 'revision':subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],cwd=repo,text=True).strip(),'sourceHashes':{str(p.relative_to(repo)):sha(p) for p in files}}
(root/(phase+'-receipt.json')).write_text(json.dumps(receipt,indent=2)+'\n')
env=dict(os.environ);env['JAVA_HOME']='/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64'
with(root/(phase+'.log')).open('w') as out:
 result=subprocess.run(cmd,cwd=repo/'core',env=env,stdout=out,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
receipt.update(exitCode=result.returncode,endedUTC=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),logSha256=sha(root/(phase+'.log')))
receipt['xml']={}
for module in ['opentaint-dataflow','opentaint-jvm-dataflow']:
 if module=='opentaint-jvm-dataflow' and phase!='full':continue
 for p in (repo/'core/opentaint-dataflow-core'/module/'build/test-results/test').glob('TEST-*.xml'):
  if phase!='full' and p.name not in ['TEST-org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.ConcreteGuideStorageTest.xml','TEST-org.opentaint.dataflow.bidi.ProtectedStorageCoordinatesTest.xml']:continue
  receipt['xml'][str(p.relative_to(repo))]={'sha256':sha(p),**ET.parse(p).getroot().attrib}
(root/(phase+'-receipt.json')).write_text(json.dumps(receipt,indent=2)+'\n')
print(json.dumps({'phase':phase,'exitCode':result.returncode,'log':str(root/(phase+'.log')),'counts':{k:sum(int(x.get(k,'0')) for x in receipt['xml'].values()) for k in ['tests','failures','errors','skipped']}}))
sys.exit(result.returncode)

selected-spec/concrete-demand-guidance-r.text:
# Concrete demand positions and protected storage

Date: 6 November 2026. Status: selected behavior; local implementation under
review. Project acceptance and the end-to-end finding gate remain open.

This specification records three user decisions: keep STAR and repair demand
guidance; do not subsume protected memberships; do not let pass rules introduce
protection. It changes the storage clauses of the
[canonical-facts proposal](../docs/design/bidirectional-canonical-facts-normal-relations-directional-inside-implementation-20261105.md).
The [implementation draft](../docs/design/bidirectional-concrete-demand-guidance-implementation-20261106.md)
describes the source changes. The
[native report](../docs/reports/bidirectional-concrete-guidance-repair-reproducer-20261106.md)
records latest reached/completed/accepted **run-5 / run-5 / run-5** for the
small example, with zero NORMAL reports. Do not treat a local storage proof
as proof of that required finding.

## 1. Scope and semantic changes

| Part | Before | Selected behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TAINT/DEMAND/ANY position | A containing MAY can remove a child position | Keep each supplied MAY position for later refinement |
| Protected membership | Coverage, E joins or fills can remove or move its flag | Keep the exact typed protected coordinate |
| Exact duplicate | Ordinary payload can already exist | Merge; protection wins and a new flag is fresh |
| Pass action | A broad action-ID test can classify it as an assignment | Transport existing protection; introduce none |

These changes affect initial-selection guidance and protection storage. They
are not only representation changes. They do not change C2 initial emission,
C5 summary restriction, fields, layers, mark identity, requests, aliases,
source/sink conditions, Target handling, ports, scheduling or stopping.
NORMAL relation coverage, opposite-record STAR matching and unprotected
EXACT/MUST/STAR DATA behavior keep their existing contracts. No raw-input
archive, new support label or history store is added.

## 2. Complete cell and effective coordinates

Fix owner, method/context, direction, block scope, physical entry and exit,
complete original premise, base and layer. Never combine different cells.
For one concrete full-mark bit, a coordinate is:

```text
K = (complete cell, field path, full mark, effective tail, effective E)

leaf.exact: effective tail = EXACT, effective E = Empty
            ignore the packet's mixed tail/E wrapper
leaf.any:   effective tail = packet tail, effective E = packet E
ANY:        effective E = Empty, as required by the existing grammar

May(X) = supplied TAINT/DEMAND/ANY leaf.any coordinates in X
H(X)   = supplied protected effective coordinates in X
```

H applies to NORMAL and DEMAND, with EXACT, ANY, STAR or MUST tails. It is
not limited to MAY guidance. Runtime GROUP atoms retain their existing
storage treatment; this change adds no FULL/GROUP eligibility filter.

For residual rows admitted by the existing relation-coverage law, each
fact-group update must satisfy:

```text
May(after) = May(before) union May(offer)
H(after)   = H(before) union H(offer)
H(after) is included at the same effective coordinates in payload(after)
```

Coalesce duplicate H only at the same effective coordinate. Different H
coordinates can share a packet, but both remain. Prefix coverage, E containment,
E intersection and complete-child filling cannot delete or relocate H.
A protected ancestor cannot remove a protected child. A protected MAY cannot
remove protected EXACT at the same point. EXACT flags deduplicate across
mixed wrappers; span flags retain their supplied tail/E.

This is a storage invariant. A real field operation or cleaner can still
kill a membership under its existing transfer rules. The invariant does not
keep facts beyond their owner or run lifetime.

## 3. Preserve incremental DATA admission

Do not re-admit the complete current state from empty. Existing STAR/T4
admission and packet normalization do not define one global normal form.
Use the same restored current DATA state and admit only the new offer:

```text
erase(X) = complete current payload packets without protection annotations
A(S,t)   = existing no-H DATA admission, with selected MAY-position retention

(dataAfter, legacyDelta) = A(restoreCurrent(erase(before)), erase(offer))
after = embedRawProtection(dataAfter, H(before) union H(offer))
```

Keep old DATA E-join carriers plain. For example, two protected MUST headers
at p with E={f} and E={g} can produce plain MUST E={}. Keep both original
protected headers too. Do not flag the derived E={} carrier.

For EXACT H, reuse an existing DATA exact coordinate once. If DATA removed
it, use an existing original cohort where possible, then an exact-only
carrier. For span H, restore the original typed header. Add the payload
carrier before attaching the mask, so factory clipping cannot remove H.

No DATA confluence or global fold-idempotence law is assumed. H union is
order independent; that fact alone does not prove all DATA effects equal.

## 4. Freshness, deltas and backends

Check ordinary DATA freshness, selected MAY-coordinate freshness and exact
H freshness. Reject only if none is fresh. A new flag is work even when its
ordinary payload already exists.

Keep legacy whole-content STAR/T4 deltas, including their exact siblings.
Filter those deltas against the new current state. Attach only current H at
the same typed coordinates. Add the remaining new H carriers. Coalesce equal
headers by raw payload/mask union; do not prefix-normalize those deltas.

The scalar and packed stores must implement this same law. Decode an affected
packed mark's current headers, restore them without re-admission, apply the
list-returning scalar update, then replace only that mark atomically. Keep
other marks unchanged. A packed FLOW-shaped geometry remains concrete TAINT
when decoded; it does not acquire the real FLOW coverage policy.

Cold packets, parent-before-child, child-before-parent, one root+child packet,
partial masks and exact duplicates all follow the same effective-coordinate
law. Publication can deliver only current memberships. It cannot revive a
legally removed plain relation. Existing FLOW replacement still applies to
unprotected rows; it cannot remove H.

## 5. Pass protection

A pass applies the ordinary AP transfer to input protection. An unprotected
input produces no new protection from that pass. This applies to CopyMark
and CopyAllMarks, in either direction and for exact or MAY targets.

PASS_THROUGH in either the action role or rule kind prevents assignment
classification. Native pass micro-edges keep their existing null action IDs.
No metadata is added to fact or micro-edge equality/hashing. Keep the existing
assignment, cleaner-survivor and generic summary-cycle protection rules.

## 6. Proof and validation boundaries

Follow [proof-guide.md](proof-guide.md). The local checked models are separate:

- `ConcreteGuidance.lean`: 58 historical MAY-only laws and unchanged C2 cells.
- `AllProtectionRetention.lean`: 35 incremental H/MAY laws with DATA admission
  as a parameter. This is not a proof of the native embedding algorithm.
- `PassProtectionPolicy.lean`: 24 pass-classification and transport laws.
- `NormalStarFlowAdmissionGap.lean`: 12 current-policy countermodel laws.
  These do not select a new admission policy or prove termination.

The models and receipts are in
[the proof directory](lean/proposals/concrete-demand-guidance-retention-20261106/README.md).
Native checks cover both storage backends, typed masks, E/header cases,
complete original/ports, handoff and pass forms. Native DATA/embedding/delta
bridges and required downstream effects need their own evidence.

The small native program now retains the previously lost child guide.
It still stops at run-5 without a NORMAL report. A getter has ANY/FLOW demand
and receives NORMAL STAR/FLOW at the same nonempty path; unchanged C2 rejects
it. This specification does not change that rule to make the gate pass.
Admitting it needs a separate semantic decision and progress check. A local
suffix-transport proof is insufficient. Project quality and post-landing
performance remain required by task.md.
